subject: proj-dy
title: (R)PROJ.DY.------GRAD.
description: Diagram closing MP(II)-19, the section on Africa as the site of the next political transformation. The prose above the diagram identifies its argument: 'the dynamics of the next transition in Africa will be very interesting for what its liberation will mean to alternative functionalism. Because the seriousness of colonial manipulation has created a necessarily complex situation for information dynamics and expansion dictates.' The crossing diagrams that complexity: (R)PROJ-DY (the reality of projection-dynamics — what actual liberation-projection consists of, on the ground) is crossed with GRAD (gradualism — the temporal pacing the colonial situation has made structurally necessary). PROJ-DY sits centrally with the subject-arrow; T-C-IMP (temporal-continuity implication) anchors the left margin, with TRS rising up-right to ALT-F (alternative form) at the top-left. INTR (introduction) sits centrally to the right of PROJ-DY as the bridging hub. POL-DY (political dynamics) and INFO-COMP (information composite) anchor the bottom-center and lower-left as subject downward outputs. GRAD sits at upper center-right as partner-axis; INT (intention) hangs to its right and MT-INFO (meta-information) anchors the right margin. CULT-AF-B (cultural-affinity base) sits centrally on the partner side. Structural argument: when projection-dynamics is crossed with gradualism, the diagonal from TRS up to ALT-F shows the subject's path through transformation into alternative-form — but ALT-F has *no edge* back to GRAD on the partner-axis. The diagonal from INT down to MT-INFO is the partner's downward chain, but MT-INFO does not reach back to INTR's central hub. INTR → CULT-AF-B is the only edge that lets the bridging hub reach the partner side — and through CULT-AF-B is the only route a liberation-projection's cultural-affinity-base can route back to the subject's POL-DY / INFO-COMP outputs. The 'necessarily complex situation' the prose names is exactly this: only the central INTR → CULT-AF-B edge holds, and it must do all the work of converting the projection's intentions into composite-information without the upper diagonals carrying the alternative-form load.
